Unless otherwise specified or the context otherwise requires, any reference to “Pure Cycle,” the “Company,” “we,” “us” or “our” is to Pure Cycle Corporation and its wholly-owned subsidiaries on a consolidated basis.
Overview
We are a diversified water and wastewater service provider, land developer, and home rental company. We provide wholesale water and wastewater services in the Denver, Colorado area, develop land we own into master planned communities, and own and lease single-family rental homes at Sky Ranch, which we plan to sell over time. Our water, wastewater and single-family rental businesses generate recurring monthly revenue, and our land development business generates revenue from lot sales and creates new long-term water and wastewater customers.
For more than 30 years, we have accumulated and continue to accumulate a portfolio of valuable water rights, land interests and single-family rental homes along the Front Range of Colorado. We have added an extensive network of wholesale water production, storage, treatment and distribution systems, and wastewater collection and treatment systems that we operate and maintain on behalf of the Rangeview District to serve domestic, commercial, and industrial customers in the eastern Denver metropolitan region.
We operate in three complementary segments – water and wastewater services, land development and single-family rental. To date, we have sold or are in the process of developing 1,535 finished lots, we have constructed and operate water and wastewater systems under our Rangeview Water Agreements (defined below) with capacity to serve approximately 2,500 residential equivalent units, and we have constructed 51 rental homes.
Our businesses are connected. Our water supplies and service rights allow us to serve the communities we develop, and each home or business built becomes a long-term water and wastewater customer that pays a one-time tap fee and monthly service charges. We typically invest in land development, water and wastewater facilities and public improvements years before the related lot sales, tap fees, service revenue and reimbursements from the Sky Ranch Community Authority Board are received. Our results also include revenue that varies with outside activity, such as water sales to oil and gas operators, and royalty income from oil and gas wells on our Sky Ranch mineral interests, which depends on third-party production and commodity prices. As a result, our revenue, earnings and cash flow can vary significantly from year to year. We estimate our water portfolio could ultimately serve approximately 60,000 SFEs; serving that number would require substantial additional infrastructure beyond our existing systems.
Business Segments
Water and Wastewater Services Segment
We own or control the water supply and infrastructure required to (i) withdraw, treat, store and deliver water; (ii) collect, treat and reuse wastewater; and (iii) treat and deliver reclaimed water for irrigation and industrial use, including non-potable irrigation of parks and open spaces.
We mainly provide wholesale water and wastewater services to local governmental entities that in turn provide residential and commercial water and wastewater services to customers in their service areas. Our largest customer is the Rangeview Metropolitan District (Rangeview District). We have the exclusive right to provide water and wastewater services to the Rangeview District’s customers in its exclusive 24,000-acre Lowry Ranch Service Area, and at Sky Ranch in the southeastern Denver metropolitan area. As of August 31, 2026, through the Rangeview District, we provide service to more than 1,800 single-family equivalent (SFE) water connections and 1,308 SFE wastewater connections. With the water rights we own and control, we believe we can serve an estimated 60,000 SFEs. See “Glossary” immediately preceding this Item 1 for the definitions of certain terms used in this report.
In addition to our domestic customers, we provide raw water for industrial oil and gas operations. Multiple operators lease more than 135,000 acres in and adjacent to our service area with more than 100 wells and miles of oil and gas collection lines. Sales of water to industrial customers in the oil and gas industry are unpredictable and fluctuate dramatically but provide high margin revenue for our water assets.

Our water and wastewater services segment generates revenue from (i) monthly metered water usage and wastewater treatment fees, (ii) one-time water and wastewater tap (connection) fees, typically payable when a building permit is issued, (iii) construction and special facility funding fees, (iv) consulting fees and (v) fees for water sold to oil and gas operators for drilling and hydraulic fracturing. Each source is described under “Our Assets – Sources of Water and Wastewater Service Revenue” below.
Land Development Segment
Through our land development segment, we develop master planned communities along the I-70 corridor of the Denver metropolitan area whose homeowners and businesses also become our water and wastewater customers. The segment allows us to capture the value our water adds to raw land along the Colorado Front Range enabling land to be entitled and developed which without water would otherwise not occur.
Our primary land asset, known as Sky Ranch, is in one of the most active development areas in the Denver metropolitan region along the rapidly developing I-70 corridor, where we are developing lots for residential, commercial, retail, and light industrial uses. Sky Ranch is zoned to include up to 3,200 single-family and multifamily homes, parks, open spaces, trails, recreational centers, schools, and over two million square feet of retail, commercial and light industrial space, all of which will be serviced by our water and wastewater services segment.
In 2010, we purchased approximately 930 acres of land along the I-70 corridor known as Sky Ranch, intending to sell lots to homebuilders and add the purchasers of the homes as our water customers. Development began in June 2017, when we entered into agreements with three national homebuilders to sell the initial residential lots (Phase 1), and has continued in Phase 2, which we have divided into Phases 2A, 2B, 2C, 2D and 2E so that we deliver infrastructure and lots to our homebuilder customers as they need them, without excess inventories of lots and homes. As of August 31, 2026, we have delivered 1,361 finished lots, including 72 lots retained for our single-family rental segment, are under construction on 154 lots (Phase 2E) scheduled for substantial completion in 2027, and have an additional 14 lots under contract for sale in 2027 at Sky Ranch. As of August 31, 2026, homebuilders have built and sold 1,021 homes at Sky Ranch, with approximately 82 additional homes under construction. All Phase 1 lots in Sky Ranch are complete and all public improvements (roads, parks, open spaces, storm drain facilities, etc.) have been accepted by the various governmental entities that will control and maintain that infrastructure.
Single-Family Rental Segment
We launched our single-family rental segment in fiscal 2021 to retain a portion of the lots we develop at Sky Ranch, contract with homebuilders to construct homes on those lots for us, and lease the homes, typically under one-year leases. As of August 31, 2026, we owned 51 rental homes, 50 of which were leased and one of which was listed for sale. During fiscal 2026, we reduced the planned size of the portfolio by reselling, or entering into contracts to resell, 19 lots previously reserved for rental homes to homebuilders, and stopped adding homes to the portfolio beyond the homes under existing construction contracts. Subsequent to fiscal 2026, our Board of Directors determined that we will not invest in new rental homes beyond our existing portfolio and existing construction contracts, and that we will sell our rental homes in an orderly manner, generally as existing leases expire. This decision reflects the returns on the portfolio in the current environment, in which our cost of capital has increased while rental rates have remained flat. Our objective is to maximize the return on our investment in the portfolio through rental income earned during the remaining ownership period and net proceeds from home sales, and we will manage the timing and pace of sales based on expected selling prices, lease expirations, and financing and operating costs. At August 31, 2026, we had contracts with a homebuilder to construct 21 additional homes on lots reserved for rental homes, and we are working with the homebuilder to reduce the number of homes completed under those contracts and to sell the related lots to homebuilders. The following section describes the material risks and uncertainties that we believe could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, and the market price of our common stock. These risks should be read in conjunction with the other information set forth in this report, including the accompanying consolidated financial statements and notes thereto. The risks described below are not the only risks we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us, or that we currently consider immaterial, could also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or the market price of our common stock.
1.
Risks Related to the Impacts the Economy and External Forces May Have on Our Operations
Our operations are concentrated in the Front Range area of Colorado; we are subject to general economic conditions in Colorado. Our assets and operations are located solely in the Front Range area of Colorado. Our performance could be adversely affected by economic conditions in, and other factors relating to, Colorado, including supply and demand for housing and zoning and other regulatory conditions. The oil and gas industry remains an important segment of the Colorado economy, and new statutes, regulations or other initiatives that limit oil and gas exploration or increase its cost, or declines in the price of oil and gas, could lead to a downturn in the Colorado economy and its housing market. To the extent that the general economic conditions in the Front Range area of Colorado deteriorate, the value of our assets, our results of operations and our financial condition could be materially adversely affected.
We are dependent on the housing market and development in our targeted service areas for future revenue. The homebuilding industry is cyclical and a deterioration in industry conditions or downward changes in general economic or other business conditions could adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition. The timing and amount of our lot sales, tap fees and water and wastewater revenue and reimbursement of our public improvement advances depend on housing developments being built near our water assets, and the development of Sky Ranch, the Lowry Ranch and other properties is subject to many factors that are outside our control, including levels of employment, consumer confidence and income, the availability of mortgage financing, interest rate levels and inflation, the cost and availability of raw materials and labor, federal and state tax and housing finance policies, immigration policy and enforcement, and tariffs on products used in construction. Rising interest rates since 2022 have significantly reduced demand for new home starts, and demand for new homes remains constrained. If development in our targeted service areas is delayed or curtailed, we could experience declines in the market value of and demand for our lots and rental homes, and we may need to use our capital resources, incur additional short or long-term debt obligations, or seek to sell additional equity, which may not be available on acceptable terms.
Significant competition from other development projects could adversely affect our results. Land development is a highly competitive business. There are numerous land developers, as well as properties and development projects, near Sky Ranch. Many of our land development competitors may have advantages over us, such as more favorable locations, which may provide more desirable schools and easier access to roads and shopping, or amenities that we may not offer, as well as greater financial resources. If other development projects are found to be more attractive to home buyers, homebuilders or other developers or operators of real estate based on location, price, or other factors, then we may be pressured to reduce our prices or delay further development, either of which could materially adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition. Our rental homes also compete with other rental housing in the Sky Ranch area, as described below.
Our water business is subject to seasonal fluctuations and weather conditions that could affect demand for our water service and our revenue and that could become more extreme with climate change. Drought and overuse may limit the availability of water to serve our customers, and such droughts may become more frequent and prolonged with climate change. Cool, wet weather, drought restrictions and our customers’ conservation efforts may reduce consumption, and freezing weather may cause pipe breakage that interrupts water transmission. Demand for our water is generally greater during warmer summer months because of irrigation and other outside water use, so cooler or wetter than expected summers may reduce our revenue. If we experience an interruption in our water supply, it could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
The physical impacts of natural disasters and severe weather conditions could reduce consumer demand for housing, result in service disruptions, delay the closing of the sale of residential lots at Sky Ranch and increase our costs, any of which could harm our sales and results of operations. We conduct our operations in the Colorado Front Range, which is subject to natural disasters, including droughts, tornadoes, wildland fires, hail, and severe weather. The occurrence of natural disasters or severe weather conditions in Colorado or elsewhere could result in interruptions in our water and wastewater operations, delay our construction activities, increase costs, and lead to shortages of labor and materials. These events may become more frequent and intense with climate change. If our
insurance or the insurance of our subcontractors does not fully cover business interruptions or losses resulting from these events, our results of operations could be adversely affected.
2.
Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
We may not generate sufficient cash flows from operations or other capital resources to pursue our business objectives. Our continuing development of Sky Ranch requires significant cash expenditures. We have advanced the Sky Ranch CAB $104.2 million for construction of public improvements in Phases 1 and 2 at Sky Ranch and we expect to advance approximately $10.8 million more for the completion of Phase 2 public improvements. Further, the Sky Ranch CAB is not required to repay us until it and the Sky Ranch Districts generate sufficient funds, as described below. We have funded and expect to continue to fund such expenditures with cash on hand, cash flows from operations and, for our rental homes, borrowings secured by those homes.
